- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction to pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model frequently overshoots in the following days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion — if true price is rising above 65, forecast often lags 1–2 days; add 1–2 points to forecast for each lagged day.
- In 30-day horizon, model underestimates upward trends when sentiment is bullish; apply a 2–5% upward bias if sentiment >0.75 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before adjustment.
